From: Maya Chen <maya.chen@helioinsurance.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@helioinsurance.com>, procurement@helioinsurance.com
Date: Thu, Mar 6, 2025 at 9:12 AM
Subject: Helio Insurance — Retention terms + compliance report pack SLA (MSA/DPA redlines)

Hi Lauren,

Following up from our procurement review: we’ve attached redlines to the MSA + DPA focused on retention and audit evidence.

Key items we need to close:
1) Data retention: Our policy requires vendor to retain Customer Data no longer than 30 days unless legally required.
2) Deletion certification: We need an attestation that customer data is deleted per configured retention within a defined window.
3) Compliance reporting pack delivery: We need an SLA for delivery (e.g., within 5 business days) once requested.
4) Audit log exports: Confirm what’s included and that exports cover admin and access events relevant to SOC 2.

Please confirm whether Redwood can accept the language as-is or propose alternates.

Thanks,
Maya
Maya Chen
Sr. Procurement Manager | Helio Insurance

Attachment: Helio_Redwood_DPA_Redlines_v2.docx

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
To: Maya Chen <maya.chen@helioinsurance.com>
Cc: Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@helioinsurance.com>, procurement@helioinsurance.com
Date: Thu, Mar 6, 2025 at 12:03 PM
Subject: Re: Helio Insurance — Retention terms + compliance report pack SLA (MSA/DPA redlines)

Hi Maya,

Thanks — received. We can meet the intent, but we’ll need a couple of adjustments so the contract aligns with how retention works across the product and with standard audit expectations.

High-level (proposed):
- We can commit that Redwood will not retain Customer Content (prompts/completions) beyond the configured retention period for the applicable data classes, subject to (a) legal hold and (b) limited security/operational exceptions that are documented and audited.
- We can provide a retention configuration export + audit-log coverage summary as part of the compliance reporting pack.
- We can provide a deletion verification statement based on system-of-record metrics (e.g., purge job success + TTL lag), rather than a per-record “certificate.”

I’m pulling in our Security/Compliance PM for exact language and the proposed SLA for the compliance pack delivery.

Best,
Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Commercial Counsel / Procurement Lead
Redwood Inference

Naomi/Aisha — Helio is asking for: (1) max 30-day retention for “Customer Data,” (2) deletion certification, (3) compliance pack SLA (5 biz days), and (4) audit log export coverage confirmation.

Can you provide: recommended contractual language that matches our retention controls (by data class) + what we can credibly commit to re: deletion verification and turnaround time for the report pack?

Forwarding their redlined docs are attached in the thread.

Lauren

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Dr. Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Mar 7, 2025 at 8:46 AM
Subject: Re: Fwd: Helio redlines — retention terms + compliance pack SLA

Lauren — recommended framing (aligned with the product):

1) Avoid the umbrella term “Customer Data” for retention. Use “Customer Content” vs “Service Data,” then define retention by data class:
- Request/response logs (metadata and payload if enabled)
- Audit logs
- Traces/metrics
- Support artifacts (tickets, attachments) if applicable

2) We should not commit to a hard 30-day maximum across all classes because audit logs are typically retained longer for security controls. Instead:
- Commit that request/response logging retention is configurable (including the ability to disable payload logging) and we’ll apply the customer’s configured retention.
- Commit that audit logs have a minimum retention period (to preserve control evidence) and are configurable above that; exact minimum depends on deployment tier.

3) Deletion certification: commit to providing evidence of enforcement (exported retention config + purge verification metrics + change history). We can commit to “commercially reasonable efforts” + a target deletion window (e.g., 7 days) for asynchronous purge jobs.

4) Compliance pack SLA: for enterprise deals, propose “within 5 business days” after request for a standard time window (e.g., last 90 days), assuming no legal hold + customer has designated contacts.

I’ll send you the current customer-facing summary doc + draft compliance pack outline to share under NDA.

Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Dir, Product — Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

From: Dr. Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Mar 7, 2025 at 9:18 AM
Subject: Re: Fwd: Helio redlines — retention terms + compliance pack SLA

+1 to Naomi’s approach.

Two guardrails to keep us out of trouble:
- Legal hold + incident response exceptions must remain (documented, access-controlled, and audited). We can commit that holds are time-bounded where possible and reviewed.
- For audit logs: we should not allow contract language that forces deletion below our minimum period because it undermines security monitoring/auditability.

I’m fine with committing to:
- Retention config export (including change history)
- Audit-log export (time-windowed) using standard templates
- A statement of purge enforcement based on automated jobs and verification metrics

Aisha
Dr. Aisha Rahman
CISO
Redwood Inference

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
To: Maya Chen <maya.chen@helioinsurance.com>
Cc: Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@helioinsurance.com>, procurement@helioinsurance.com
Date: Fri, Mar 7, 2025 at 2:27 PM
Subject: Re: Helio Insurance — Retention terms + compliance report pack SLA (MSA/DPA redlines)

Hi Maya,

Thanks again — we reviewed internally (Security + Product). We can meet the business intent, but we need to adjust the redlines so the obligations map to specific data classes and preserve minimum audit logging needed for security controls.

Proposed edits (summary):

A) Retention language
Instead of “no longer than 30 days for Customer Data,” we propose:
1) “Customer Content” (prompts/completions and related request payloads where stored) is retained only for the period configured by Customer for the applicable data class, and Redwood will apply the configured retention settings.
2) For service-generated “Audit Logs,” Redwood retains logs for a minimum period necessary for security and compliance controls (cannot be reduced below minimum), and provides export functionality; retention above the minimum is configurable.
3) Legal hold and security incident exceptions remain permitted, but will be access-controlled and logged.

B) Deletion verification / attestation
We propose replacing per-record deletion certification with a standard evidence package including:
- Retention configuration export (by data class) + change history
- Purge/TTL enforcement verification metrics (e.g., TTL lag, purge success/failure rates)
- Audit-log export for a requested time window

C) Compliance reporting pack SLA
We can commit to: “Redwood will provide the baseline compliance reporting pack within five (5) business days of Customer’s written request,” for standard windows (e.g., last 90 days) and assuming no active legal hold that would restrict disclosure.

D) SOC 2 / attestations
We can provide our SOC 2 Type II report under NDA (attached here as a placeholder; if you prefer, we can share via your secure portal).

I’m attaching a short retention controls overview + a draft outline of the compliance reporting pack (customer version). If helpful, we can also schedule 20 minutes with your security reviewer to walk through audit-log export coverage (admin access, role changes, policy changes, export events, etc.).

If you confirm the above is acceptable, I’ll mark up the redlines accordingly and return a clean/proposed redline set.

Best,
Lauren

Attachment: Redwood_Retention_Controls_Overview_20250307.pdf
Attachment: Redwood_Compliance_Reporting_Pack_Baseline_v0.9.pdf
Attachment: Redwood_SOC2_TypeII_2024.pdf (NDA-required)

Date: Tue, Mar 11, 2025 at 4:38 PM
Subject: Re: Helio Insurance — Retention terms + compliance report pack SLA (MSA/DPA redlines)

Hi Lauren,

This is directionally fine.

Two follow-ups to get this closed:
1) Can you explicitly state the “target deletion window” after TTL expiry (you mentioned asynchronous jobs)? Our template asks for “within 7 days.”
2) For the compliance reporting pack SLA: please include language that Redwood will provide it in a customer-shareable format suitable for audit review (PDF + CSV exports are fine) and that it includes (i) retention settings export, (ii) audit log export, and (iii) access control/RBAC summary.

If you can incorporate those in the redlines, we can route for final signature.

Thanks,
Maya
